stories.title: North Carolina food pantries report rising demand amid SNAP cuts
stories.summary_or_snippet: North Carolina Health News reported that federal SNAP cuts and new work requirements are pushing more people toward food pantries, while pantry leaders said rising demand is becoming increasingly difficult to meet.

stories.approved_why_it_matters: The source reports more people turning to food pantries in North Carolina and providers saying the rising demand is becoming harder to meet.
stories.approved_uncertainty_note: County-specific examples in the article should remain attributed as local context rather than generalized statewide evidence.
stories.evidence_text:
Federal SNAP cuts and new work requirements are pushing more people toward food pantries, with North Carolina SNAP participant rolls shrinking by more than 110,000 since September 2025.

“The food pantries are being used as a backstop rather than an emergency,” Loyd continued. “We’re seeing a lot more people, and it’s getting increasingly more difficult to meet the need.”
